title: Review of reacting thermals (SIMDE): replicates on fresh seeds 7 and 8; the g=0 twin and the fuel fork reproduce on seed 7; Supported for S, I, M, D with E by construction
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py unchanged with labkit (128^2, 600 frames, spf 25, t=600) on fresh seeds 7 and 8, and on seed 7 its g=0 twin and the fuel fork at t=400. Both fresh seeds look like the claim's sheets: the hot noise burns out, and crescent caps riding their own vortex pairs rise into fresh fuel, shed arms and multiply to ~18-30 caps. Persistent splits 34 and 38, max generation 7 and 6, merge/split 0.19 and 0.21. The claim's divmove.py finds 15 of 21 and 17 of 24 dividing caps (born by a split, ending in a persistent split) that travel at least 3 sqrt(area) between their own birth and their own division (6/21 and 3/24 in long-axis lengths), mostly upward (18/21, 20/24 within 45 deg of up). The g=0 twin on seed 7 makes still round spots that divide (13 persistent splits, gen 2) with 0 of 7 dividing spots passing. In the fork every body goes out within 2 t (20 -> 3 -> 0 at t=400-402; fed run 18 at t=600).

observations.S: rerun/seed7/sheet.png and rerun/seed8/sheet.png t=0: a random hot field over the whole box on uniform fuel
observations.I: rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=81-600: separate crescent caps, each with a burnt wake; dividing caps live 54-200 t from their birth to their own division with the crescent body plan (rerun/seed7/divmove.json); labkit counts no track alive >= 50% of the run because caps divide every ~60-200 t
observations.M: rerun/seed7/divmove.json: 15/21 dividing caps travel >= 3 sqrt(area) between own birth and own division (crescents moving broadside, which the protocol allows), seed 8 17/24; g0/seed7/divmove.json: 0/7, max 1.6 sqrt(area)
observations.D: rerun/seed7/FACTS.md: 34 persistent splits, generation 7, merge/split 0.19; rerun/seed8/FACTS.md: 38, generation 6, 0.21; T=0 is absorbing in world.py (r needs T > Tc), so caps come from caps
observations.E: fork/seed7/metrics.json series n_comp: 20 bodies at t=400, 3 at t=401, 0 from t=402 to 600; rerun/seed7 (fed, same seed): 17-19 at t=401-405, 18 at t=600

seeds_run.result: pass: 34 persistent splits, gen 7, 15/21 dividing caps >= 3 sqrt(area), g=0 twin 0/7, fork 20 -> 0 in 2 t
pass: 38 persistent splits, gen 6, 17/24 dividing caps >= 3 sqrt(area)

controls_run.M: g0/seed7 (g 0, same seed, grid, duration): still round spots, 0/7 dividing spots pass 3 sqrt(area)

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (heat is made only by burning and decays at h=0.3, so a fuel cut must put every body out within a few 1/h); it counts for the rung under mechanism. M is buoyant rise along a fixed axis set by a uniform gravity; I count it because the buoyancy exists only while the cap burns (heat decays in ~3 t, caps travel for 50-200 t) and the g=0 twin loses it, but the operator may judge gravity an imposed field. In long-axis lengths only 6/21 and 3/24 pass. Bodies are hot spots in a fluid with no conserved matter. I did not run dt/2 or a grid variant (the claim's dt/2 is at the world step); one fork seed and one g=0 seed.
